claimsMade.text: AFFIRMATIVE EVIDENCE AGAINST THE ACCOUNT, NOT MERELY AN ABSENCE. Klass records: 'Stone claims that he and his Army team were sent to the USAF Bentwaters base in England in late December of 1980 to investigate a UFO incident... A further challenge to this claim is that on Dec. 23, 1983, Stone made a Freedom Of Information Act (FOIA) request to the USAF for information on the Bentwaters UFO incident which he would have acquired during his (alleged) official visit in 1980. Further, Stone's request used his home address and did not show that he was an Army sergeant.' This is an act by Stone, three years after the event, inconsistent with his own later account of having been there officially.

Klass states the source: 'If Greer had obtained a copy of Stone's military record from the National Personnel Records Center in St. Louis, he could have learned that these and other such Stone claims were FALSE.' The assignments as Klass prints them: entered the Army 8 July 1968; after basic training 'he was trained to be a clerk/typist'; Vietnam February 1970 to August 1972 'where his duties are listed as clerk/typist'; Fort Gordon and Fort Knox, principal duty clerk/typist; 'as of March 1975 his duty is shown as administration specialist'; August 1976 to August 1983 in Germany as administration specialist; then Keesler AFB and Fort Gordon as 'Det. Sgt'; and from May 1985 the New Mexico Military Institute as 'chief administrative clerk'. The underlying NPRC record itself was not opened by this board, which is why this is Tier 2 and not Tier 1.

label: Philip J. Klass
narrative: Philip J. Klass is load-bearing on this board in at least two clusters now, and building him once here saves every later pass from citing an unnamed sceptic. His Skeptics UFO Newsletter #68 of Summer 2001 is the contemporaneous critical record of the Disclosure Project's press conference, and it does two things no other opened document does: it prints Clifford Stone's assignment history, which Klass obtained from the National Personnel Records Center in St. Louis, and it quotes the FAA Alaskan Region's press release of 5 March 1987 and the air traffic control transcript on JAL 1628 at length. He is an interested party and he is a rigorous one about his own limits: he states in the same issue that he did not attend the press conference, that Greer had refused him admission to a similar event in 1997 and reportedly refused the Fund For UFO Research, and that his account of the event therefore rests on Greer's press releases, on Greer's 573-page book and on broadcast footage. That declared limitation applies to his reporting of the event and does not touch the records he obtained himself, and the board should keep the two apart. He is not a disinformation actor and no edge on this board should imply it.
